principles: A headline cannot settle a doctrine.
A tradition's internal disagreement should remain visible.
Technology can change the stage without proving the script.

christianCore.title: Shared Christian horizon
christianCore.summary: Across historic Christian traditions, the shared center is shorter than the charts: Jesus Christ will return, the dead will be raised, judgment is real, and God's future is not reducible to technological progress.

christianPerspectives.name: Dispensational / pre-trib
christianPerspectives.commonIn: Influential in American evangelical and nondenominational settings; not the only evangelical view.
christianPerspectives.emphasis: Keeps Israel and the church distinct in the prophetic timetable and expects the church to be caught up before a future tribulation.
christianPerspectives.techResonance: Global systems of deception, commerce, identity or control may feel especially salient because Revelation 13 is often read futuristically.
christianPerspectives.guardrail: A new payment system, AI agent, biometric tool or political institution is not therefore 'the mark' or a fulfilled prophecy.

christianPerspectives.name: Historic premillennial
christianPerspectives.commonIn: Found across older evangelical and patristic streams.
christianPerspectives.emphasis: Christ returns before a future millennial reign, but the church is not removed from history by a separate secret pre-tribulation rapture.
christianPerspectives.techResonance: New systems may be evaluated as possible instruments of persecution, deception or empire without being treated as a countdown clock.
christianPerspectives.guardrail: Technological resemblance to apocalyptic imagery does not establish chronology.

christianPerspectives.name: Amillennial
christianPerspectives.commonIn: Common in Catholic, Lutheran, Reformed and Orthodox-influenced readings, with important internal differences.
christianPerspectives.emphasis: The 'thousand years' is typically read symbolically as the present reign of Christ rather than a future earthly political period.
christianPerspectives.techResonance: AI, surveillance or political concentration can be read as recurring patterns of idolatry, empire, deception or domination rather than a newly discovered missing puzzle piece.
christianPerspectives.guardrail: The point is faithfulness in every age, not proving that the current news cycle uniquely starts the clock.

christianPerspectives.name: Postmillennial
christianPerspectives.commonIn: A minority view today, especially present in some Reformed and reconstructionist circles.
christianPerspectives.emphasis: Expects the gospel's historical influence to expand substantially before Christ's return.
christianPerspectives.techResonance: Exponential tools can be interpreted either as instruments that may serve human flourishing and mission or as counterfeit forms of dominion detached from repentance and truth.
christianPerspectives.guardrail: Technological progress is not identical to the kingdom of God.

christianPerspectives.name: Partial preterist
christianPerspectives.commonIn: Present in some Reformed and Anglican circles and compatible with more than one millennial view.
christianPerspectives.emphasis: Reads a substantial portion of Matthew 24 and Revelation's judgment imagery against first-century Jerusalem and Rome while retaining a future return of Christ.
christianPerspectives.techResonance: Tends to resist treating every technological development as a novel prophetic fulfillment because much apocalyptic language is read in its first-century setting.
christianPerspectives.guardrail: A strong historical reading does not make contemporary ethical questions about technology irrelevant.

otherHorizons.name: Sunni Islamic last-hour traditions
otherHorizons.emphasis: The Qur'an and hadith traditions contain last-hour expectations including deception, the return of Jesus (Isa), resurrection and judgment.
otherHorizons.techResonance: Powerful systems that deceive, simulate authority or demand misplaced trust may be discussed through Dajjal or shirk themes.
otherHorizons.guardrail: No current technology by itself identifies the Dajjal or dates the Hour.

otherHorizons.name: Twelver Shia horizon
sequence: Return of Isa in last-day tradition
otherHorizons.emphasis: The hidden twelfth Imam is expected to return as al-Mahdi in a future restoration of justice.
otherHorizons.techResonance: Technological power can be judged through themes of tyranny, deception and justice rather than treated as proof of the Mahdi's timetable.
otherHorizons.guardrail: Political or technical upheaval does not identify the awaited Imam.

otherHorizons.name: Jewish messianic horizons
otherHorizons.emphasis: Jewish traditions differ significantly, but many retain hope for a messianic age, justice, peace and restoration.
otherHorizons.techResonance: Technology may be assessed through justice, idolatry, human dignity and repair of the world rather than a single end-times chart.
otherHorizons.guardrail: Judaism does not have one universally agreed apocalyptic sequence.

otherHorizons.name: Hindu cyclical horizons
otherHorizons.emphasis: Many Hindu traditions frame history cyclically rather than as one linear apocalypse, with diverse teachings about yugas and divine restoration.
otherHorizons.techResonance: Acceleration, craving, disorder or claims of mastery may be read through dharma / adharma rather than through a Christian-style prophetic timetable.
otherHorizons.guardrail: Hindu traditions are highly diverse; no single yuga interpretation should be treated as universal.

otherHorizons.name: Buddhist future horizons
sequence: Decline / preservation of Dharma in some traditions
otherHorizons.emphasis: Buddhist traditions generally do not center a creator-led final judgment; impermanence, craving and liberation are more central, with Maitreya expectations in many schools.
otherHorizons.techResonance: AI attachment and endless personalized stimulation can be examined as new objects of clinging and craving.
otherHorizons.guardrail: That analogy is interpretive, not a claim that Buddhist texts predicted AI.

otherHorizons.name: Secular / exponential futures
otherHorizons.emphasis: Forecasts about AGI, automation, longevity or collapse are hypotheses and scenarios rather than revealed eschatology.
otherHorizons.techResonance: The future can still take on quasi-religious language: salvation, extinction, transcendence, immortality, singularity.
otherHorizons.guardrail: A forecast is not scripture, and a capability curve does not settle meaning.
